task: Set the privileged-EXEC enable secret to EnableLabSecret8 on this isolated lab router.

teaching.hint: The enable credential is separate from a user’s login secret.
teaching.takeaway: This protects entry through enable. It does not create a local login account or encrypt a remote terminal session.

task: Create local user admin with privilege level 15 and the lab secret AdminLabSecret8.

teaching.hint: The username, initial privilege and secret are separate parts.
teaching.takeaway: The account can start an EXEC session at privilege 15 when local authentication uses it. Creating the account alone does not make the VTY lines use the local database.

task: The lab uses the conventional hostname/domain/RSA workflow. R1 is already named; set its local domain to lab.test.

teaching.hint: This is device identity for key generation, not a DNS-server setting.
teaching.takeaway: The domain participates in the conventional RSA-key identity workflow. No DNS lookup or external DNS server is required to generate the lab key.

task: R1 has its hostname and domain configured and supports the general-keys form. Generate a 2048-bit RSA key pair for the lab SSH server.
answer: crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 2048

teaching.hint: Specify RSA and the requested modulus in bits.
teaching.takeaway: Key generation supplies cryptographic keys; it does not configure user authentication or VTY transport. Other IOS images may use an interactive modulus prompt.

syntax.text: crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus

task: R1’s SSH keys exist. Configure the server to accept SSH version 2 only.

teaching.hint: Set the protocol version independently of line transport.
teaching.takeaway: Verify the reported version with show ip ssh. An enabled SSHv2 server can still be unreachable or refused by the VTY policy.

task: R1 provides exactly VTY lines 0 through 4. Select all of those remote terminal lines so you can apply the SSH login policy.

teaching.hint: Select the virtual terminal lines, not the physical console.
teaching.takeaway: The prompt becomes R1(config-line)#. The supplied range covers this router; on another device, inspect the actual VTY ranges and apply the intended policy to all of them.

task: The selected VTY lines must authenticate against R1’s existing local username database. Configure that authentication method.

teaching.hint: A shared line password and the local user database use different login forms.
teaching.takeaway: Local authentication needs a valid username and secret already present. Keep console recovery available and test a fresh login before ending the working session.

task: The selected VTY lines currently permit Telnet and SSH. Allow SSH as their only incoming terminal transport.

teaching.hint: Choose the permitted transport; do not change the login database.
teaching.takeaway: This removes Telnet from the permitted incoming transports on these lines. Apply the intended policy to every actual VTY range, then test a new SSH session.

task: A new login succeeds, but the user reaches > instead of the intended # prompt. Report this session’s current privilege level.

teaching.hint: Inspect the authenticated session’s privilege, not SSH server status.
teaching.takeaway: A level-1 result means authentication succeeded with lower privilege. Investigate the account and authorization settings separately from network reachability.

task: On the selected terminal lines, disconnect an idle EXEC session after five minutes and zero seconds.

teaching.hint: The timeout takes minutes first, then seconds.
teaching.takeaway: The setting applies to idle EXEC time, not a login-attempt timeout. Setting both values to zero would disable idle expiry.

task: Before testing a new login, display R1’s SSH server state and configured protocol version.

teaching.hint: Inspect the SSH service rather than the table of logged-in users.
teaching.takeaway: An enabled version-2 server is one prerequisite. Reachability, permitted VTY transport and valid credentials still need a fresh session test.

task: An administrator has opened a new remote terminal session. Display the terminal-session table showing logged-in users and their lines.

teaching.hint: Choose current sessions rather than the SSH server’s capabilities.
teaching.takeaway: Match the user and line, and inspect the source location where shown. This is session evidence; it does not verify that every unused VTY line has the correct policy.
